docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures and attaches a file-based logger instance for an individual CLI execution run. It creates a target directory specified by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs), sanitizes the project name and generation mode against unwanted characters, and establishes a uniquely timestamped log file named {safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log. Any existing handlers (such as the import-time NullHandler) are cleared from logger, and a new logging.FileHandler formatted with %(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s is registered.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): Identifier of the target repository or project. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): Pipeline operation mode (e.g., "tutorial", "architecture"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative filesystem path of the initialized .log file.

Raises: * OSError: If directory creation or log file access fails due to filesystem permission constraints.

Implementation: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

The function performs input sanitation on project_name by replacing non-alphanumeric and non-whitelisted characters (-, _, .) with underscores. It also replaces hyphens in mode with underscores. Once the FileHandler is established, the function immediately writes execution boundary headers containing metadata to verify output capture before returning the file path to the caller (such as main).

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Loads and deserializes the persisted JSON prompt-response cache from llm_cache.json. If the file does not exist, is corrupted, or fails to parse, it logs a warning and returns an empty dictionary.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping raw prompt strings to cached LLM response text strings, or an empty dictionary if loading fails.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; all file I/O and JSON decoding errors are intercepted internally.

Implementation & Usage: 

def load_cache():
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")
    return {}

The function provides a fault-tolerant fallback mechanism for local development caching. Any underlying I/O errors (e.g., FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, or json.JSONDecodeError) are caught silently and flagged using logger.warning, returning a fresh dictionary to prevent crashing LLM pipeline execution.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes and writes the provided in-memory cache dictionary back to the llm_cache.json file on disk.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The dictionary mapping prompt strings to LLM response strings to persist.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; file writing and serialization exceptions are handled internally.

Implementation & Usage: 

def save_cache(cache):
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to save cache")

The method opens cache_file in write mode and executes json.dump. If an exception occurs during serialization or file writing (for instance, disk full conditions or restricted write permissions), a warning is logged to llm_logger while allowing overall pipeline execution to continue uninterrupted.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the active LLM provider strategy from environment variables. If LLM_PROVIDER is explicitly set, its value is returned. If omitted, it falls back to checking whether GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY are defined, returning "GEMINI" if either is present.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: The resolved provider string (e.g., "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", "OLLAMA"), or None if unresolvable.

Implementation & Usage: 

def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This function acts as the runtime provider selector for the application. It establishes Google Gemini as the implicit default when relevant API credentials exist in .env, while allowing overrides via explicit LLM_PROVIDER environment variable assignments (such as "OPENROUTER" or "OLLAMA").

docs.title: _get_openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Queries OpenRouter's public /api/v1/models catalog to inspect capabilities, supported reasoning effort parameters, and metadata for a specific model ID. Caches the response payload in the module-level variable _openrouter_models_cache to eliminate redundant HTTP requests across calls.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The model identifier string (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

Returns: * dict | None: A dictionary containing model metadata if located within the catalog; otherwise, None.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; network and timeout errors result in populating an empty cache list and returning None.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function optimizes network bandwidth and prevents rate limiting by fetching OpenRouter model data only on the initial call. It leverages Python's next() built-in with a generator expression to locate the model object matching model_id.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum token context window supported by a given endpoint and model name combination. Automatically allocates a 1,000,000-token limit for Gemini endpoints, dynamically extracts context limits from OpenRouter's model catalog for OpenRouter URLs, and defaults to 100,000 tokens for all other providers or when lookups fail.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Base URL or endpoint of the LLM provider. * model_name (str): Name or ID of the target model. * api_key (str, optional): API key parameter (optional, defaults to "").

Returns: * int: The context length limit in tokens.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; errors fall back safely to 100000.

Implementation & Usage: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This helper is primarily utilized during prompt chunking, file aggregation, and token budgeting across the indexing pipeline. When operating against Gemini endpoints or models containing "gemini" in their name, it returns a 1,000,000-token window. When hitting OpenRouter endpoints, it dynamically queries the model registry to retrieve exact token limits.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches chat completion requests to OpenAI-compatible provider endpoints such as OpenRouter or Ollama. Dynamically resolves environment variables based on LLM_PROVIDER (e.g., <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, <PROVIDER>_API_KEY), formats messages under the /v1/chat/completions REST specification, applies reasoning/thinking effort payloads, executes HTTP requests with robust timeout limits, and validates response schemas.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The input user prompt text to send to the LLM. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity ("low", "medium", or "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The generated text response extracted from choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL) are missing, if invalid JSON is returned, or if the choices attribute is missing from a 200 OK response. * Exception: Wrapper exception providing diagnostic context on HTTP errors, connection drops, request timeouts, or general network failures.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            print(f"\033[93mWarning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}\033[0m")
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

This function implements a generic REST integration for OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints. It maps provider-specific reasoning flags (e.g., verifying supported_efforts via OpenRouter metadata or attaching think / reasoning_effort fields for Ollama) and automatically adjusts model temperature to 1.0 when reasoning effort is enabled. It configures a dual connection and read timeout (timeout=(10, 300)) to accommodate long generation runs and includes defensive JSON validation to catch upstream provider errors hidden within 200 OK responses.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Direct execution handler for the Google GenAI SDK (google.genai). Supports both Vertex AI authentication (via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION) and standalone Google Developer API keys (via GEMINI_API_KEY). Formats reasoning configurations by translating string levels into explicit token budgets (low: 1024, medium: 4096, high: 8192), filters non-text thought signatures from output candidate parts, and returns pure text output.

Parameters: * prompt (str): User prompt text to execute against Gemini. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning budget intensity ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The combined text generated by the model candidates, or an empty string if no content parts are returned.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY are found in the environment.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

The function instantiates the official genai.Client, choosing Vertex AI mode when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set and API Key mode otherwise. When thinking_level is provided, it configures types.ThinkingConfig with explicit token budgets to ensure compatibility with models such as gemini-3.7-flash. To prevent downstream logging warnings regarding non-text internal parts (such as thought_signature), it iterates over response.candidates[0].content.parts to filter and join only valid text segments.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public entry point for dispatching prompts to LLMs throughout the application. Handles token counting via count_tokens, logs prompt metadata and payload details, coordinates local disk cache hits and misses, measures round-trip inference latency, routes requests to _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider, and stores newly generated responses in the cache.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete prompt string to submit to the model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and update the local JSON cache. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning level ("low", "medium", "high"), or None for standard generation. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual response generated by the LLM (or retrieved from cache).

Raises: * ValueError: If provider resolution fails or if underlying provider calls fail. * Exception: Any network or provider-level errors encountered during an uncached invocation.

Implementation & Usage: 

def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text

Example from Module Self-Test: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

    # First call - should hit the API
    print("Making call...")
    response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
    print(f"Response: {response1}")

call_llm serves as the single orchestrator for all generation tasks across the framework. It ensures consistent token counting via utils.token_utils, audit logging to the run log configured in configure_logging, latency metrics, and atomic cache operations.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/call_llm.py

Following the package initialization established in init.py, utils/call_llm.py provides the core model invocation layer for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It abstracts external Large Language Model (LLM) communications across multiple backend providers, manages disk-backed prompt-response caching, resolves context window limits, and normalizes reasoning and thinking parameter configurations.

docs.title: Core Responsibilities
docs.text:
1. Multi-Provider Dispatching: Supports native Google Gemini APIs (via the official google-genai SDK for both Vertex AI and direct API key authentication) and generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (such as OpenRouter, Ollama, LocalAI, and vLLM).
  2. Deterministic Response Caching: Manages an on-disk JSON key-value store (llm_cache.json) indexed by the exact input prompt string, avoiding duplicate API calls and redundant token consumption during repeated pipeline executions.
  3. Context Length Discovery: Dynamically resolves context window capacities per model by querying remote endpoints (e.g., OpenRouter metadata APIs) or applying rule-based heuristics based on endpoint URLs and model names.
  4. Reasoning Parameter Translation: Maps abstract reasoning effort tiers (low, medium, high) to backend-specific schemas, such as Gemini's token-based thinking budget (ThinkingConfig), OpenRouter's reasoning payload (reasoning.effort), and Ollama's think/reasoning_effort payload fields.
  5. Defensive Error Handling and Logging: Provides structured logging through a dedicated "llm_logger" instance configured with a NullHandler at import time, preventing root logger pollution before runtime initialization by main.py.

docs.title: Module-Level State and Configuration
docs.text: The module maintains internal configuration variables and global in-memory caches to optimize repeated calls within a single process execution.

docs.title: Environment & Logger Setup
docs.text:
# Load environment variables from .env file
load_dotenv()

# Configure logging - deferred until main.py calls configure_logging()
# At import time, set up logger with NullHandler (no file output yet)
logger = logging.getLogger("llm_logger")
logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
logger.propagate = False  # Prevent propagation to root logger
logger.addHandler(logging.NullHandler())  # Absorb logs until configured

# Simple cache configuration
cache_file = "llm_cache.json"

# Cache for model capabilities to avoid repeated API calls
_openrouter_models_cache = None
  • logger: An isolated logging.Logger instance named "llm_logger". Setting propagate = False and binding a NullHandler prevents unformatted output from leaking into standard error before main.py explicitly configures console/file formatters.
  • cache_file: Points to the default relative file path "llm_cache.json" in the current working directory, used for local response persistence.
  • _openrouter_models_cache: A process-level global cache initialized to None. When querying OpenRouter for model capabilities or context window boundaries, the fetched array of model metadata objects is cached in this variable to eliminate repeated remote HTTP GET calls.

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Reads and deserializes the JSON cache file from the file path specified in cache_file. If the file does not exist, cannot be opened, or contains invalid JSON data, the function catches the exception, logs a warning via logger.warning(), and returns an empty dictionary. This ensures that a missing or corrupted cache file does not crash the pipeline.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * dict: A mapping of prompt strings to their cached LLM string outputs, or an empty dictionary {} on read failure.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated. All file I/O and JSON decoding errors are swallowed and logged.

Implementation: 

def load_cache():
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")
    return {}

The function provides an operational safeguard for filesystem access. When running concurrent pipeline steps or starting with a clean repository without a pre-existing cache file, load_cache() recovers cleanly by returning an empty in-memory hash table.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes the provided cache dictionary to disk as a JSON structure at cache_file. The file is opened in write mode ("w"), completely overwriting the previous cache state. Any I/O errors encountered during disk access or serialization are caught and logged as warnings, preventing cache write failures from terminating active pipeline execution.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The updated dictionary containing prompt keys and response text values to persist.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated. All disk write errors are caught and logged.

Implementation: 

def save_cache(cache):
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to save cache")

The routine performs an atomic write over the designated path. While sufficient for single-threaded or standard synchronous operations, downstream workers share this global cache file across execution stages. If disk write permissions fail or the underlying volume is read-only, pipeline execution continues uninterrupted while emitting non-blocking warnings to the log stream.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Determines the active LLM backend provider by inspecting the system environment variables. The function checks for an explicit LLM_PROVIDER environment variable (e.g., "OLLAMA", "OPENROUTER"). If LLM_PROVIDER is unset or empty, it falls back to inspecting Google Gemini-specific configuration keys: if either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY is present, it returns "GEMINI".

Parameters: None.

Returns: * str | None: The resolved provider identifier string ("GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", "OLLAMA", etc.), or None if no relevant configuration keys are detected.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Implementation: 

def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This resolution logic establishes Gemini as the default backend if Google Cloud credentials exist, while allowing runtime overriding via LLM_PROVIDER. It serves as the primary discriminator used by call_llm() to route requests between the Google GenAI SDK and generic OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints.

docs.title: _get_openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Fetches and caches model metadata from OpenRouter's public endpoint (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models). If the module-level _openrouter_models_cache is unpopulated (None), it dispatches an HTTP GET request with a 5-second timeout and extracts the "data" array. It then performs a linear search over the cached models to return the dictionary whose "id" matches model_id.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The unique model identifier string (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet", "meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct").

Returns: * dict | None: The model capability dictionary containing pricing, context limits, and reasoning capability objects, or None if the model ID is not found or the network request fails.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated. Network errors or invalid JSON payloads result in an empty list cache [], returning None.

Implementation: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The memoization pattern used here avoids repeated network latency when making hundreds of inference calls against OpenRouter. By storing the parsed metadata in _openrouter_models_cache, subsequent lookups for reasoning capabilities and context limits execute in memory.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum input context window size (in tokens) for a given model and endpoint combination. It applies a hierarchical resolution strategy: 1. If endpoint_url is empty, returns the default baseline of 100,000 tokens. 2. If endpoint_url contains "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" or model_name contains "gemini" (case-insensitive), returns 1,000,000 tokens. 3. If endpoint_url contains "openrouter.ai", queries the OpenRouter /api/v1/models endpoint (with a 5-second timeout) to extract the model's exact context_length. 4. If remote queries fail or the endpoint is unknown, catches any exception, logs a warning, and falls back to 100,000 tokens.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): The base or full URL of the model inference service. * model_name (str): The identifier of the target model (e.g., "gemini-3.7-flash", "qwen/qwen-2.5-coder-32b"). * api_key (str, optional): API authentication key (unused in the current implementation, defaults to "").

Returns: * int: The maximum supported context length in tokens.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised. Network or parsing failures default to 100,000.

Implementation: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Fetch the maximum context length of a model based on the endpoint.
    If endpoint is Gemini API, safely default to 1,000,000 tokens.
    If endpoint is openrouter.ai, make GET to /api/v1/models and extract.
    Default to 100,000.
    """
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This context length calculation is consumed upstream by partitioning and token management routines in token_utils.py to calculate chunk sizes and prompt truncation thresholds before dispatching prompts to external LLMs.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an inference request against an OpenAI-compatible REST completions endpoint (e.g., OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM). The function dynamically determines environment variable names from the LLM_PROVIDER setting (reading {provider}_MODEL, {provider}_BASE_URL, and {provider}_API_KEY), validates required configuration values, builds the request payload, adapts reasoning/thinking parameters, and sends an HTTP POST request to {base_url}/v1/chat/completions.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete prompt string to transmit. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), or None to disable explicit reasoning configurations.

Returns: * str: The textual content generated by the model extracted from response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].

Raises: * ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, {provider}_MODEL, or {provider}_BASE_URL is missing from the environment; if the provider returns invalid non-JSON content; or if an HTTP 200 response lacks the expected "choices" field. * Exception: Wraps underlying requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout, and requests.exceptions.RequestException errors with descriptive diagnostic messages.

Implementation: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    // ... [Read and validate {provider}_MODEL, {provider}_BASE_URL, {provider}_API_KEY] ...

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0  # Required for many reasoning models
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit_raw
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Warning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}", dest="STDOUT")
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        // ... [Format error details and wrap exception] ...
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

The function handles edge cases across third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoints: - Connection & Timeout Management: Uses a split connection/read timeout (10, 300) via requests.post(), allowing 10 seconds for initial connection negotiation and up to 300 seconds for complete token generation on long responses. - Provider-Specific Reasoning Handling: For OpenRouter, it validates requested reasoning levels against supported_efforts from metadata lookups and sets temperature: 1.0 (required by many reasoning models like OpenAI o-series or DeepSeek-R1). For Ollama, it sets both think and reasoning_effort fields to accommodate different Ollama daemon versions. - Defensive Error Handling: Detects and handles edge cases where proxy servers return an HTTP 200 OK status code with an internal JSON error object or rate-limiting message instead of a valid choices array.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entry point for all LLM inference in the system. It handles token tracking, cache validation, provider routing, performance timing, and cache updates: 1. Calculates prompt token length using count_tokens from token_utils.py. 2. Logs execution metadata (provider, model, thinking level, cache flag, and prompt token count). 3. When use_cache=True, checks load_cache() for an existing prompt match. On a cache hit, returns the stored response immediately. 4. On a cache miss or when caching is disabled, records the start timestamp and routes the prompt to either _call_llm_gemini() (if get_llm_provider() == "GEMINI") or _call_llm_provider() (for all other providers). 5. Logs request duration and response character counts. 6. When use_cache=True, saves the updated prompt-response pair to disk via save_cache().

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full prompt text to send to the language model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and update the local JSON cache. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level ("low", "medium", "high"), or None. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The complete string output returned by the LLM.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables or configuration keys are missing. * Exception: If underlying network calls, authentication, or API endpoints fail.

Implementation: 

# By default, we use Google Gemini 3.7 flash, as it shows great performance for code understanding
def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text

The function uses localized imports (import time, from utils.token_utils import count_tokens) inside the function body to reduce top-level module import overhead and prevent circular dependency cycles with modules like token_utils.py. The logging output includes clear delimiting headers ('=' * 80) and token counts to assist in debugging and tracing pipeline runs.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches inference requests directly to Google Gemini models using the official google-genai SDK (google.genai.Client). It configures authentication using one of two strategies: 1. Vertex AI Authentication: If GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set, instantiates genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=..., location=...) using GEMINI_LOCATION (defaulting to "us-central1"). 2. Direct API Key Authentication: If GEMINI_API_KEY is set, instantiates genai.Client(api_key=...).

If neither variable is found in the environment, it raises a ValueError. The target model is read from GEMINI_MODEL (defaulting to "gemini-3.7-flash"). When thinking_level is specified, it maps the level to a concrete token budget (low -> 1024, medium -> 4096, high -> 8192) via types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget) inside a types.GenerateContentConfig. Finally, it executes client.models.generate_content() and concatenates all text parts from the response candidates, safely ignoring non-text parts (such as thought_signature).

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt for the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): The reasoning depth ("low", "medium", "high"), or None.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text output from the model's response parts.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment. * google.genai.errors.APIError: If Google's API returns an error during content generation.

Implementation: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

This implementation handles the multi-part content stream returned by reasoning models such as Gemini 2.0 and Gemini 3.7 Flash Thinking. Rather than calling response.text directly (which raises library warnings when non-text artifacts like thought signatures are included), it filters response.candidates[0].content.parts to extract and join only parts where part.text is not None.

docs.title: Standalone Execution Block
docs.text:
The module includes a standard __main__ guard allowing developers to test LLM connectivity and caching behavior directly from the command line without running the full pipeline:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

    # First call - should hit the API
    print("Making call...")
    response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
    print(f"Response: {response1}")

docs.title: Execution Mechanics
docs.text: When executed directly (python utils/call_llm.py), the script: 1. Loads environment variables from the local .env file via load_dotenv(). 2. Initializes the test prompt string "Hello, how are you?". 3. Calls call_llm() with use_cache=False, bypassing the cache to verify live API credentials, network connectivity, and model availability. 4. Outputs the returned response text directly to standard output.

docs.title: Error Handling & Resilience Matrix
docs.text:
The following matrix summarizes how call_llm.py handles various runtime errors across different providers:

Failure Mode Trigger Condition Component Handling System Impact Missing Cache File llm_cache.json does not exist on disk load_cache() catches exception, logs warning, returns {} Non-Fatal: Cache miss occurs; executes live API request. Corrupted Cache File Invalid JSON syntax in llm_cache.json load_cache() catches exception, logs warning, returns {} Non-Fatal: Disregards cache; executes live API request. Missing Provider Config LLM_PROVIDER not set and no Gemini keys _call_llm_provider() / _call_llm_gemini() raise ValueError Fatal: Aborts current pipeline node execution. Missing Base URL / Model {provider}_BASE_URL or {provider}_MODEL empty _call_llm_provider() raises descriptive ValueError Fatal: Aborts inference with explicit error. Invalid REST Response JSON HTTP endpoint returns non-JSON text / HTML emit_raw("WARNING", ...) and raises ValueError Fatal: Logs raw response; raises error up the stack. Malformed 200 OK Response API returns 200 OK but payload omits "choices" Identifies missing key, logs error_detail, raises ValueError Fatal: Prevents KeyError crashes downstream. HTTP Errors (4xx / 5xx) Upstream API rate limits (429) or server errors Extracts error details from JSON payload and raises Exception Fatal: Propagates structured diagnostic details. Network Connection / Timeout Host unreachable or execution exceeds 300s Catches ConnectionError / Timeout and wraps with context Fatal: Suggests checking connectivity / endpoint status. Gemini Thought Signature Gemini thinking parts present in response Filters parts for part.text is not None before joining Non-Fatal: Safely ignored; returns clean response text.

docs.title: utils.crawl_github_files
docs.text: utils/crawl_github_files.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module provides repository ingestion capabilities for GitHub repositories within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It is designed to extract codebase contents across public and private repositories, handling two distinct ingestion paths based on the input URL format:

  1. SSH Git Cloning Mode: Activated when the target URL starts with git@ or ends with .git. It clones the repository into an isolated temporary directory via GitPython (git.Repo.clone_from), walks the local directory structure, enforces file inclusion/exclusion and .gitignore rules using pathspec, and reads text content directly from disk.
  2. GitHub REST API Mode: Activated for standard HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/ref/path). It parses the URL into structural components (owner, repository name, branch or tree SHA, and targeted subdirectory path). It queries the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}), handles dynamic branch and commit tree resolution, fetches repository-level .gitignore rules, performs automatic rate-limit backoff using HTTP headers (X-RateLimit-Reset), and downloads raw or base64-encoded file payloads.

Both paths enforce strict file size filtering (max_file_size), text-encoding checks (handling UTF-8 with BOM and binary file detection), glob pattern matching via fnmatch, path rebasing (use_relative_paths), and return a normalized dictionary mapping file paths to their string contents alongside crawl statistics.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url, token=None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Serves as the primary public entry point for extracting text files from a remote GitHub repository. The function standardizes pattern collections, detects whether to utilize SSH cloning or the GitHub REST API, evaluates inclusion/exclusion patterns alongside .gitignore path specifications, downloads or reads files under the size threshold, and compiles a comprehensive execution summary.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): The remote URL of the GitHub repository. Supports full HTTPS tree paths (e.g., https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/commit_hash/sub/path) or SSH URLs (e.g., git@github.com:owner/repo.git). * token (str, optional): GitHub personal access token used to authorize private repository access and lift public REST API rate limits. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowed size in bytes per file (default is 1 MB: 1048576 bytes). Files exceeding this limit are skipped. * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True, returns dictionary keys stripped of the leading subdirectory path specified in the URL. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns (e.g., "*.py", {"*.md", "*.txt"}) indicating which file names should be retained. If None, all files are candidates. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns indicating which file or directory paths should be skipped.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing two keys: * "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of resolved file paths to their decoded string file content. * "stats" (dict): Execution metadata containing counts of downloaded files, skipped files, active filter patterns, and base path configurations.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the provided HTTP URL cannot be split into at least owner and repo components. * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are hit without an authorization token provided.

Example: 

# Extract from example usage in utils/crawl_github_files.py
repo_url = "https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/6c38dc93f40a47f4d1350adca9ec0d72502e223f/pydantic"

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=github_token,
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 MB in bytes
    use_relative_paths=True,  # Enable relative paths
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},  # Include Python and Markdown files
)

files = result["files"]
stats = result["stats"]

The function normalizes inputs into sets, sets up pattern matching closures, and dynamically routes between temporary disk cloning via Git and in-memory REST API tree traversal. When operating in REST API mode, it resolves branch names and commit SHAs dynamically, falling back to repository defaults when no tree parameters are supplied in the URL.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file matches the current execution criteria based on file name glob inclusions, repository .gitignore specifications, and explicit path exclusions.

Parameters: * file_path (str): The relative path of the file within the repository or cloned working tree. * file_name (str): The base name of the file (e.g., main.py). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec, optional): Compiled gitignore rules specifier instantiated using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines('gitwildmatch', ...). Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file satisfies include filters, does not match .gitignore, and is not excluded by exclude_patterns; otherwise False.

Example: 

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The inclusion evaluation follows a three-stage gating sequence. First, if include_patterns is populated, the file's basename must match at least one pattern via fnmatch.fnmatch. Second, if a compiled gitignore_spec is provided, gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path) checks the full relative path; any match immediately disqualifies the file. Finally, if exclude_patterns is defined, the full relative path is matched against all exclusion globs.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API endpoint /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches to obtain a list of all remote branches available on the target repository. This information is used to match multi-part branch names (e.g., feature/branch-name) present within complex repository URLs.

Parameters: * owner (str): The GitHub account or organization name hosting the repository. * repo (str): The repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: A list of branch descriptor dictionaries returned by GitHub's API, or an empty list [] if the repository was not found or an HTTP error occurred.

Raises: * Exception: Raised if HTTP status code 403 or 429 is received and no GitHub token was configured.

Example: 

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get brancshes of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable."
                )
            else:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository."
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function transmits an authorized GET request with a strict 30-second connection and read timeout. It verifies status codes, explicitly separating rate-limit exhaustion (403/429), missing or unauthorized repositories (404), and general server or network errors before parsing JSON results.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively fetches and processes directory contents and files from the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}). It handles rate-limit backoff, skips excluded directories and oversized files, downloads raw file contents via download_url or decodes base64 content blocks, and populates the outer files dictionary.

Parameters: * path (str): Repository-relative subdirectory or file path to query against the GitHub Contents API.

Returns: * None: Mutates the enclosing scope's files dictionary and api_counters state in-place.

Raises: * Exception: Raised if unauthenticated rate limits are encountered during directory retrieval.

Example: 

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            print(f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            // ... [Handle 404 and branch warning messages]
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

        contents = response.json()
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]
            // ... [Calculate rel_path, check filters, download raw/base64 content, recurse dirs]

fetch_contents performs recursive crawling over the GitHub API tree. If a rate limit is reached for an authenticated user, it inspects the X-RateLimit-Reset Unix timestamp from GitHub's response headers, suspends execution via time.sleep, and retries the request automatically upon expiration. For each item returned, if the entry is a directory, it checks inclusion/exclusion patterns before executing a recursive call. If it is a file, it checks file size constraints, issues a download request via download_url (or falls back to decoding base64-encoded strings directly from the JSON metadata), and writes decoded text directly into the outer files dictionary.

docs.title: crawl_github_files.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/crawl_github_files.py

Following the inference and model interaction mechanics established in call_llm.py, crawl_github_files.py provides the remote codebase ingestion engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository analysis pipeline. It extracts source code trees, documentation, and configuration files directly from remote GitHub repositories without requiring manual pre-cloning by the user.

docs.title: Key Architectural Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Dual Traversal Strategies:
  2. SSH Shallow Clone Mode: Automatically invoked when repository URLs use SSH syntax (git@...) or terminate in .git. It clones the target repository into an ephemeral directory via tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and git.Repo.clone_from(), walking the local filesystem via os.walk() to eliminate API quota consumption.

  3. GitHub REST API Mode: Used for standard HTTP/HTTPS GitHub URLs (including deep links pointing to subtrees or branches). It queries the GitHub REST API v3 (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}), handling directory recursions, single-file downloads, and base64 blob payload decompression.

  4. Branch, Tree, and Path Disambiguation:

  5. Inspects deep-link URLs structured as https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/tree/{ref}/{path}.

  6. Resolves nested branch names containing forward slashes (e.g., feature/login-system) versus raw commit SHAs and Git tree objects by querying /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches and /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}.

  7. Multi-Tier Filtering Engine:

  8. .gitignore Parsing: Dynamically fetches or reads .gitignore from the root of the repository and constructs a pathspec.PathSpec matcher utilizing gitwildmatch rules.
  9. Pattern Matching: Evaluates user-defined include_patterns and exclude_patterns using Unix shell-style wildcards (fnmatch.fnmatch).

  10. Size & Binary Guardrails: Enforces a strict byte-size ceiling (max_file_size) and catches binary encoding exceptions (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) to protect downstream LLM token context windows.

  11. Resilient Rate Limiting & Telemetry:

  12. Monitors GitHub API HTTP response headers for rate-limiting status codes (403, 429). When rate limits are encountered with authenticated sessions, it extracts X-RateLimit-Reset, sleeps until the reset epoch, and retries the operation.
  13. Integrates with utils.output (emit, emit_raw, get) to publish structured CLI events for file tracking, exclusions, directory skips, and summary tallies.

Visibility: Public Signature: 

def crawl_github_files(
    repo_url: str,
    token: str | None = None,
    max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths: bool = False,
    include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
    exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:

Description: Coordinates the entire extraction lifecycle for remote GitHub repositories. It sanitizes input patterns, identifies the transport mechanism (SSH local clone vs. HTTPS REST API), handles authentication and rate limiting, executes file filtering against gitignore specifications and glob patterns, and returns a dictionary of valid text files alongside ingest statistics.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Target repository URL. Can be an SSH clone address (git@github.com:org/repo.git), a standard HTTPS URL (https://github.com/org/repo), or a deep link to a specific commit/branch and directory (https://github.com/org/repo/tree/branch_name/sub/dir). * token (str | None, optional): GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT). Required for private repositories and recommended for public repositories to elevate API rate limits from 60 to 5,000 requests per hour. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Upper file size limit in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. Defaults to 1048576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True and crawling a subdirectory via deep links, strips the base path prefix so returned keys are relative to that subdirectory. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Shell-style glob patterns specifying which file names to include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.md"}). Defaults to None (includes all files). * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Shell-style glob patterns specifying file or directory paths to exclude. Defaults to None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing: * "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of repository relative paths to their raw text content. * "stats" (dict[str, Any]): Ingestion metrics, including "downloaded_count", "skipped_count", "skipped_files", "base_path", "include_patterns", "exclude_patterns", and optional transport source info ("source").

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if repo_url cannot be parsed into valid GitHub owner and repository segments. * Exception: Raised if GitHub API rate limits are exceeded and no token is supplied to authenticate the session.

# Implementation excerpt from utils/crawl_github_files.py
    # Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    # Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

    if is_ssh_url:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

            # ... os.walk directory traversal and filtering ...
            return {
                "files": files,
                "stats": {
                    "downloaded_count": len(files),
                    "skipped_count": 0,
                    "skipped_files": [],
                    "base_path": None,
                    "include_patterns": include_patterns,
                    "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
                    "source": "ssh_clone",
                },
            }

    # Parse GitHub URL to extract owner, repo, commit/branch, and path
    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
    path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip("/").split("/")
    if len(path_parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")
    # ... REST API traversal setup ...

The function normalizes include/exclude pattern arguments into Python sets to ensure fast and consistent membership testing. When an SSH URL is detected, it delegates execution to GitPython's git.Repo.clone_from() inside a managed temporary directory context manager, guaranteeing that all downloaded repository artifacts on disk are cleaned up upon function exit or error. If an HTTPS URL is provided, it parses URL path segments to initialize REST API traversal.

Example:

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN"),
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True,
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},
)

files = result["files"]
stats = result["stats"]

def should_include_file(
    file_path: str,
    file_name: str,
    gitignore_spec: pathspec.PathSpec | None = None
) -> bool

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file should be ingested or ignored based on a three-tier predicate evaluation: inclusion pattern matching, .gitignore rule conformance, and exclusion pattern matching.

Parameters: * file_path (str): Relative repository path of the file (e.g., src/utils/parser.py). * file_name (str): Basename of the file (e.g., parser.py). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): Compiled pathspec instance representing active .gitignore rules. Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion or gitignore rules; False otherwise.

# Implementation from utils/crawl_github_files.py
    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The function prioritizes include patterns by matching file_name against include_patterns via fnmatch.fnmatch. If the file matches (or if no include patterns are configured), it passes the full file_path to gitignore_spec.match_file(). If the path is not ignored by git rules, it performs a final check against exclude_patterns. This multi-stage check prevents downloading or reading unnecessary test files, build artifacts, or secret configurations.

            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]
            # ... path relativization, file processing, dir recursion ...
        return None

The function handles directory responses (represented as JSON lists) and single-file responses (represented as JSON objects normalized into single-element lists). When downloading file payloads, it prefers the direct download_url CDN link. If download_url is absent, it falls back to decoding the base64-encoded content block in the JSON response.

# File handling and base64 fallback excerpt from fetch_contents()
            if item["type"] == "file":
                # ... pattern and size checks ...
                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if file_response.status_code == 200:
                        files[rel_path] = file_response.text
                        api_counters["processed"] += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                else:
                    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if content_response.status_code == 200:
                        content_data = content_response.json()
                        if content_data.get("encoding") == "base64" and "content" in content_data:
                            file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                            files[rel_path] = file_content
                            api_counters["processed"] += 1
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)

Directory recursion evaluates both .gitignore rules and exclude_patterns against directory basenames and relative paths before triggering network requests. This optimization prevents unnecessary traversal of large directories like node_modules, venv, or .git.

# Directory recursion excerpt from fetch_contents()
            elif item["type"] == "dir":
                dir_excluded = False
                dir_reason = None
                if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(rel_path):
                    dir_excluded = True
                    dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                if not dir_excluded and exclude_patterns:
                    dir_name = item["name"]
                    for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                        dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                        if fnmatch.fnmatch(item_path, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_name, dir_pattern):
                            dir_excluded = True
                            dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                            break
                if dir_excluded:
                    api_counters["entry"] += 1
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=api_counters["entry"], path=rel_path, reason=dir_reason)
                    continue
                fetch_contents(item_path)

Example: 

# Entrypoint kick-off inside crawl_github_files
fetch_contents(specific_path)

docs.title: Error Handling & Edge Cases
docs.text: Scenario Detection Mechanism Resolution / System Action Private Repository (Unauthenticated) HTTP 404 on API endpoint Emits an error explaining that private repositories require a GitHub token via --token or GITHUB_TOKEN. API Rate Limit Exceeded (With Token) HTTP 403/429 with "rate limit exceeded" Reads X-RateLimit-Reset, sleeps until the reset epoch, and retries the request. API Rate Limit Exceeded (No Token) HTTP 403/429 without Token Raises a descriptive Exception prompting the user to supply credentials. Binary / Non-UTF8 Files UnicodeDecodeError / ValueError on decode Increments count_non_text, skips the file, and logs CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT. File Exceeds Size Limit file_size > max_file_size Increments count_size_limit, skips downloading the payload, and logs CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT. Branch with Forward Slashes URL containing tree/feature/name Enumerates /branches to find the longest matching prefix before extracting the subdirectory path.

docs.title: utils.crawl_local_files
docs.text:
utils/crawl_local_files.py

As the local filesystem counterpart to utils.crawl_github_files, this module provides directory traversal, file filtering, and content extraction capabilities for repositories stored locally on disk. It produces an output dictionary structure matching the remote GitHub crawler ({"files": {filepath: content}}), ensuring seamless interoperability across the ingestion pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text: The module traverses local directories using a single-pass os.walk strategy with in-place directory pruning. During traversal, it respects git-ignore rules, glob inclusion/exclusion patterns, and file size limits, while safely extracting UTF-8 text content and discarding binary files.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. .gitignore Integration: Automatically detects and compiles repository-level .gitignore files using pathspec (with gitwildmatch syntax) to prune ignored paths before traversal.
  2. Directory Pruning: Mutates dirs in-place during os.walk execution to prevent traversing into excluded directory trees (e.g., .git, virtual environments, or node_modules).
  3. Filtering Pipeline: Applies exclusion patterns, inclusion filters, and size constraints sequentially to minimize unnecessary I/O operations.
  4. Encoding & Binary Safety: Reads file contents using utf-8-sig to automatically strip byte-order marks (BOM) while capturing UnicodeDecodeError and general exceptions to skip binary assets.
  5. ANSI Console Reporting: Emits formatted, color-coded logging for each encountered item and outputs a structured summary table at the end of the crawl process.
